answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before it can submit work, and earns it back only after an independent, randomly selected peer validates a useful result. Validation is sampled from peers whose own bonds are at risk, so rubber-stamping exposes them to slashing too. A sybil operator must therefore lock capital across many identities and pay real losses when caught; making a delta of fake accounts is not free, even if they drift through a glacier of activity or hide in a nebula of aliases.
